key_insight: Gaussian process PDE solvers can incorporate linear inequality constraints by sequentially conditioning first on the PDE/equality data and then on a finite-dimensional constraint event, yielding a valid non-Gaussian posterior.
engineering_relevance: This lets engineers enforce physically or financially admissible solutions such as nonnegativity, monotonicity, and no-arbitrage without redesigning the underlying PDE solver.
method: Condition a GP prior on PDE residuals, boundary data, and observations to obtain a physics-informed posterior.
Treat virtual inequality constraints as a finite-dimensional event and update the equality posterior using truncated-Gaussian moments.
Use the resulting non-Gaussian posterior directly; no change is needed to the PDE-conditioning step or the inequality-update step.
evidence_signal: Across Poisson, option-pricing, and air-quality benchmarks, the constrained posteriors improved constraint satisfaction and often reduced error, including a 63% error drop for 2D Poisson under monotonicity and a reduction of calendar-arbitrage from 10% to 1% on thinned S&P 500 options.
watch_item: The approach relies on finite virtual constraint points and truncated-moment computation, so scalability and constraint placement may become important in higher-dimensional or tightly constrained problems.
paper_title: Constrained Probabilistic Numerics: Gaussian Process Solvers for Linear PDEs under Linear Inequality Constraints
